sources.pageTitle: Evaluate AI automation and voice agents for your business
sources.text: Choose a bounded first job Consider appointment intake, routing a common enquiry, or drafting a follow-up for staff review. Write down what the system may answer and what it must pass to a person. Treat an impressive demonstration as the start of evaluation, not proof that it will handle your entire business.

sources.pageTitle: Evaluate AI automation and voice agents for your business
sources.text: Test voice calls your team actually receives Build a test set with unclear names, background noise, changed appointments, unavailable times, interruptions, and a request for a person. Check the resulting calendar entry or CRM record, not only the spoken response. Set a fallback when the calendar or phone integration is unavailable. Bring your business, not a guess. Talk through your payment setup, website, or next automation. Free Profit Leak Analysis

sources.pageTitle: Evaluate AI automation and voice agents for your business
sources.text: Control access and review errors Use the smallest access scope needed for the pilot. Require approval for financial commitments, account changes, and sensitive decisions. NIST provides a voluntary framework for evaluating and managing AI risks; it does not certify a particular voice agent or guarantee reliability. Sources: NIST AI Risk Management Framework

sources.pageTitle: Evaluate AI automation and voice agents for your business
sources.text: Decide whether to expand Track completed tasks, wrong answers, transfers, staff corrections, and the time spent reviewing the pilot. Compare these with the current workflow using the same definitions. Expand only after the owner agrees the results justify the cost and operational responsibility.

sources.text: Breadcrumb Home Guides AI automation & voice agents What should I check before connecting an AI agent to my CRM? KCG field guide · Nationwide What should I check before connecting an AI agent to my CRM? Define exactly which CRM records the agent may read, create, or update before connecting it. Use limited access and test with non-production records. Require review for sensitive changes and verify how duplicates, failures, and retries are handled. Assign a person to monitor the integration and revoke access when it is no longer needed. Free Profit Leak Analysis Book a call By Keystone Consulting Group Last reviewed 2026-10-28 Sources: NIST AI Risk Management Framework

sources.pageTitle: What should I check before connecting an AI agent to my CRM?
sources.text: Specify permitted actions List the required fields and operations for the pilot. Distinguish drafting a note from changing a customer record or triggering outreach. Ask the provider to demonstrate the proposed permission settings and the record of changes, instead of granting broad access to simplify setup.

sources.pageTitle: What should I check before connecting an AI agent to my CRM?
sources.text: Test failure and recovery Include unavailable services, duplicate requests, incomplete input, and conflicting customer records. Check that an interrupted task does not silently create duplicates when retried. Define how staff can identify, correct, and pause a problem before permitting unattended updates. Bring your business, not a guess. Talk through your payment setup, website, or next automation. Free Profit Leak Analysis

sources.pageTitle: What should I check before connecting an AI agent to my CRM?
sources.text: Frequently asked questions Should the agent receive administrator access? Ask for the minimum permissions required for the agreed workflow and a demonstration that broader access is unnecessary. What should happen when the CRM is unavailable? Specify a visible failure or review queue and an approved retry process. The agent should not claim a record was saved when it was not.

sources.text: Breadcrumb Home Guides AI automation & voice agents When should an AI voice agent transfer to a person? KCG field guide · Nationwide When should an AI voice agent transfer to a person? Define handoff rules before launch: a caller asks for a person, the agent lacks an approved answer, a required system is unavailable, or the conversation involves an exception outside its authority. Test the transfer and the fallback if nobody answers. Staff should receive enough context to continue without making the caller start over. sources.pageTitle: When should an AI voice agent transfer to a person?
sources.text: Write the boundary in plain language List what the agent may confirm, what it may only collect for review, and what it must escalate. Include disputes, requests to change account access, unusual scheduling needs, and any question your team considers sensitive. Do not leave the escalation decision entirely to a vague instruction to be helpful.

sources.pageTitle: When should an AI voice agent transfer to a person?
sources.text: Test the receiving side Check the destination, operating hours, missed-transfer behavior, and summary delivered to staff. Use an approved test scenario to confirm that a failed transfer does not produce an invented promise. Review the fallback with the person responsible for returning the call. Bring your business, not a guess. Talk through your payment setup, website, or next automation. Free Profit Leak Analysis

Should staff see a summary? Specify the minimum useful context and review its accuracy during the pilot. Limit the information to what staff need for that task.

sources.pageTitle: California: dual pricing and credit-card surcharge rules
sources.text: Breadcrumb Home Guides Payment processing California: dual pricing and credit-card surcharge rules KCG field guide · Nationwide California: dual pricing and credit-card surcharge rules Short answer: California’s SB 478 generally requires advertised consumer prices to include mandatory fees. The Attorney General says an avoidable credit-card fee generally is not mandatory, but a fee is mandatory when a business only accepts credit cards. Dual pricing and surcharging still need separate review under applicable laws and card-network rules. Free Profit Leak Analysis Book a call By Keystone Consulting Group Last reviewed 2026-10-28 Sources: California DOJ: SB 478 FAQ Visa: US merchant surcharge Q&A Not legal advice. This is general information from the linked sources, reviewed October 28, 2026. Laws and network rules can change. Have your legal adviser and acquirer review your actual pricing, locations, and checkout before implementation.

sources.pageTitle: California: dual pricing and credit-card surcharge rules
sources.text: The payment options change the advertised-price analysis SB 478 took effect July 1, 2024. California’s DOJ FAQ says a card processing fee generally is not mandatory when the customer can avoid it by paying another way, such as cash. If credit cards are the only accepted payment method, the fee must be included in the advertised price. Do not describe SB 478 as a blanket ban on all surcharges. Sources: California DOJ: SB 478 FAQ

sources.pageTitle: California: dual pricing and credit-card surcharge rules
sources.text: Check scope and the food-service exception The FAQ addresses most goods and services for personal use and identifies exclusions, including commercial-use transactions. SB 1524 provides a specific exception for certain food and beverage sellers when mandatory fees are conspicuously displayed wherever prices appear. A restaurant should review that exception directly rather than applying a general retail checklist. Sources: California DOJ: SB 478 FAQ Bring your business, not a guess. Talk through your payment setup, website, or next automation. Free Profit Leak Analysis

sources.pageTitle: California: dual pricing and credit-card surcharge rules
sources.text: Review the complete checkout Ask counsel to review the applicable pricing laws and proposed payment options. Separately ask the acquirer to review network restrictions, debit exclusions, disclosures, and rate limits. Test product pages, menus, invoices, and receipts against the approved approach. An optional payment fee is not automatic permission to ignore other requirements. Sources: Visa: US merchant surcharge Q&A California DOJ: SB 478 FAQ

sources.pageTitle: California: dual pricing and credit-card surcharge rules
sources.text: Frequently asked questions Does SB 478 prohibit every credit-card fee? No. The DOJ FAQ distinguishes fees that customers can avoid with another payment method from mandatory fees when only credit cards are accepted. Can I disclose a mandatory fee only at checkout? For transactions covered by the general rule, the advertised price must include mandatory fees. Review any specific statutory exception separately.

sources.pageTitle: How does a cash discount program work for a restaurant?
sources.text: Breadcrumb Home Guides Payment processing How does a cash discount program work for a restaurant? KCG field guide · Nationwide How does a cash discount program work for a restaurant? A restaurant cash discount program gives customers a lower price when they pay cash instead of the displayed card price. Dual pricing shows both prices before payment. Review menus, signs, checkout screens, and receipts together, then have your provider review the setup for your locations before training staff or changing prices. Free Profit Leak Analysis Book a call By Keystone Consulting Group Last reviewed 2026-11-09 Sources: Visa: US merchant surcharge Q&A Not legal advice. This is general information from the linked sources, reviewed October 28, 2026. Laws and network rules can change. Have your legal adviser and acquirer review your actual pricing, locations, and checkout before implementation.

sources.pageTitle: How does a cash discount program work for a restaurant?
sources.text: Start with a restaurant checklist Bring the customer’s complete ordering and payment path to the review. List dine-in, takeout, online ordering, and telephone payments. Check the prices on menus, signs, and checkout screens. Ask for demonstrations of cash, credit, debit, tips, and refunds. Request the full processing, gateway, and equipment proposal.

sources.pageTitle: How does a cash discount program work for a restaurant?
sources.text: Distinguish a discount from an added fee A genuine cash discount reduces the displayed card price. Dual pricing displays cash and card prices side by side. Adding a fee to a posted price may be treated as a surcharge regardless of the label. Review the existing dual-pricing and surcharge guides with your provider before choosing the presentation. Sources: Visa: US merchant surcharge Q&A Bring your business, not a guess. Talk through your payment setup, website, or next automation. Free Profit Leak Analysis

sources.pageTitle: How does a cash discount program work for a restaurant?
sources.text: Rehearse service before launch Ask the provider to show how the proposed setup handles a split bill, a tip, a void, and a partial refund. Have staff explain the displayed prices before payment. Compare the menu, terminal total, and receipt in each scenario, and resolve inconsistencies before serving customers under the new setup.

Review the actual menu, checkout, and receipt presentation with your provider. Can the same setup cover online orders? Confirm each channel separately. Ask your provider to demonstrate the prices customers see before payment and the resulting receipt for online orders as well as in-person service.

sources.text: Use a short selection checklist Give each consultant the same business requirements so their proposals can be compared. Request a statement review and a complete written proposal. sources.pageTitle: What does a merchant services consultant do, and how do I choose one?

sources.text: Breadcrumb Home Guides Payment processing Colorado: dual pricing and credit-card surcharge rules KCG field guide · Nationwide Colorado: dual pricing and credit-card surcharge rules Short answer: Colorado’s enacted SB21-091 permits a credit-card surcharge within a framework of 2% of the transaction or the actual merchant discount fee. It requires notice and excludes debit, cash, check, and gift-card payments. Card-network limits still apply. Have the acquirer document the permitted calculation and presentation for your proposed setup. Free Profit Leak Analysis Book a call By Keystone Consulting Group Last reviewed 2026-10-28 Sources: Colorado SB21-091, enacted summary Visa: US merchant surcharge Q&A Not legal advice. Have your legal adviser and acquirer review your actual pricing, locations, and checkout before implementation.

sources.pageTitle: Colorado: dual pricing and credit-card surcharge rules
sources.text: Do not flatten the rule into one universal cap The enacted summary describes a limit of 2% of the transaction or the merchant discount fee, defined as the actual fee paid to process it. It does not support describing Colorado as an unconditional permission to pass through any amount. Ask for review of the chosen calculation and supporting records. Sources: Colorado SB21-091, enacted summary

sources.pageTitle: Colorado: dual pricing and credit-card surcharge rules
sources.text: Include the notice and exclusions The act requires notice on the premises or, for online purchases, before the transaction is completed. It excludes debit cards, gift-card redemption, cash, and checks. Include these payment types in the provider’s configuration review and request sample receipts. Sources: Colorado SB21-091, enacted summary Bring your business, not a guess. Talk through your payment setup, website, or next automation. Free Profit Leak Analysis

Confirm the final approved rate and disclosures for the card brands and channels you accept. Sources: Visa: US merchant surcharge Q&A

sources.pageTitle: Is dual pricing legal?
sources.text: Breadcrumb Home Guides Payment processing Is dual pricing legal? KCG field guide · Nationwide Is dual pricing legal? Dual pricing can be lawful when the displayed cash and card prices, checkout behavior, and receipts follow applicable law and card rules. It is not a universal exemption from surcharge restrictions. A fee added to a posted price may be a surcharge regardless of its name. Review each location before implementation. sources.text: Breadcrumb Home Guides Google Business Profile & SEO Will FAQ schema get my business rich results or AI citations? KCG field guide · Nationwide Will FAQ schema get my business rich results or AI citations? FAQ schema describes visible questions and answers, but it does not guarantee a rich result or an AI citation. Google currently limits FAQ rich results to well-known authoritative government and health websites. A business should use accurate markup that matches its page and focus on genuinely useful answers rather than a promised search enhancement. sources.text: Breadcrumb Home Guides Payment processing Maine: dual pricing and credit-card surcharge rules KCG field guide · Nationwide Maine: dual pricing and credit-card surcharge rules Short answer: Maine’s Title 9-A, section 8-509 prohibits seller surcharges for credit or debit cards and defines a discount from the regular price as outside that surcharge definition. The statute includes a specific governmental-entity exception. Private businesses should review displayed prices and payment logic rather than treating that exception as general permission. Free Profit Leak Analysis Book a call By Keystone Consulting Group Last reviewed 2026-10-28 Sources: Maine Title 9-A §8-509 Visa: US merchant surcharge Q&A Not legal advice. sources.pageTitle: Maine: dual pricing and credit-card surcharge rules
sources.text: Both credit and debit are named in the statute Maine defines a surcharge as increasing the regular price for a cardholder when the same increase is not imposed on someone paying cash, check, or similar means. The prohibition explicitly names both credit and debit. Review what your regular price is and when a customer learns it. Sources: Maine Title 9-A §8-509

sources.pageTitle: Maine: dual pricing and credit-card surcharge rules
sources.text: A reduction is different from an added charge The statute says a discount or reduction from the regular price is not a surcharge. sources.pageTitle: Maine: dual pricing and credit-card surcharge rules

sources.text: Breadcrumb Home Guides AI automation & voice agents How do I measure whether an AI pilot is worth keeping? sources.text: Define the baseline Choose a representative set of tasks and record how the current team handles them. Decide what counts as completion and which mistakes are unacceptable. Record manual review time during the pilot so apparent time savings do not hide a new supervision workload.

sources.text: Breadcrumb Home Guides Payment processing What is next-day funding? KCG field guide · Nationwide What is next-day funding? Next-day funding generally describes access to eligible payment proceeds on the next business day, subject to the provider’s settlement and payout process. KCG offers next-day funding availability, not an unconditional deposit guarantee. Confirm eligibility, batch cutoff, weekends, bank timing, and any holds in writing before using a deposit date for cash-flow planning. sources.pageTitle: How much can a business surcharge a credit card?
sources.text: Breadcrumb Home Guides Payment processing How much can a business surcharge a credit card? KCG field guide · Nationwide How much can a business surcharge a credit card? For US Visa credit transactions, the surcharge cannot exceed the lower of the applicable merchant discount rate or 3%. Mastercard publishes a separate cost-based rule with a 4% maximum. State restrictions and cross-brand conditions also matter. Do not choose a rate from a headline cap without reviewing your actual acceptance costs. Free Profit Leak Analysis Book a call By Keystone Consulting Group Last reviewed 2026-10-28 Sources: Visa: US merchant surcharge Q&A Mastercard: merchant surcharge rules New Jersey Consumer Affairs: surcharge FAQ Colorado SB21-091, enacted summary Not legal advice. This is general information from the linked sources, reviewed October 28, 2026. Laws and network rules can change. Have your legal adviser and acquirer review your actual pricing, locations, and checkout before implementation.

sources.pageTitle: How much can a business surcharge a credit card?
sources.text: A network maximum is not your permitted rate Visa’s rule ties the fee to the applicable merchant discount rate, with 3% as the ceiling. Mastercard distinguishes brand-level and product-level surcharges. Its published maximum does not establish what a merchant accepting several networks may charge across all cards. Sources: Visa: US merchant surcharge Q&A Mastercard: merchant surcharge rules

sources.pageTitle: How much can a business surcharge a credit card?
sources.text: Check state limits and evidence New Jersey limits the surcharge to the seller’s actual cost. Colorado’s enacted rule provides a 2% or actual merchant discount fee framework. Have the acquirer document the approved calculation for your setup and schedule a review when processing costs or network rules change. Sources: New Jersey Consumer Affairs: surcharge FAQ Colorado SB21-091, enacted summary Bring your business, not a guess. Talk through your payment setup, website, or next automation. Can I apply Mastercard’s maximum to Visa? No. Each network has its own rules, and multi-brand acceptance adds conditions. Ask your acquirer to approve the complete setup.

sources.pageTitle: Can I surcharge debit cards?
sources.text: Breadcrumb Home Guides Payment processing Can I surcharge debit cards? KCG field guide · Nationwide Can I surcharge debit cards? No. Visa and Mastercard prohibit surcharges on their debit and prepaid cards under their US surcharge rules. Selecting credit at the terminal does not turn a debit card into a credit card. Ask your processor to demonstrate automatic card-type detection and verify that debit and prepaid payments receive no surcharge. Free Profit Leak Analysis Book a call By Keystone Consulting Group Last reviewed 2026-10-28 Sources: Visa: US merchant surcharge Q&A Mastercard: merchant surcharge rules Not legal advice. This is general information from the linked sources, reviewed October 28, 2026. Laws and network rules can change. Have your legal adviser and acquirer review your actual pricing, locations, and checkout before implementation.

sources.pageTitle: Can I surcharge debit cards?
sources.text: The card type controls the rule Visa explicitly says a debit card remains a debit card when the customer selects credit, which refers to signature versus PIN processing. Mastercard also excludes its debit and prepaid cards from permitted surcharges. Do not train staff to decide eligibility from the button a customer presses. Sources: Visa: US merchant surcharge Q&A Mastercard: merchant surcharge rules

sources.pageTitle: Can I surcharge debit cards?
sources.text: Test every channel Request evidence of card-type handling for your terminal, payment link, keyed entry, website, and recurring billing workflow before enabling a surcharge. Include voids and refunds in the test plan. If a proposed setup cannot reliably exempt ineligible cards, do not approve that setup. Bring your business, not a guess. sources.pageTitle: Do I need to register or give notice before surcharging?
sources.text: Breadcrumb Home Guides Payment processing Do I need to register or give notice before surcharging? KCG field guide · Nationwide Do I need to register or give notice before surcharging? Visa requires notice to your acquirer at least 30 days before surcharging. Mastercard’s older summary also describes advance notice, but its current registration page says US web registration is not presently required while rules are updated. Confirm the current network and acquirer process in writing before enabling any surcharge. Free Profit Leak Analysis Book a call By Keystone Consulting Group Last reviewed 2026-10-28 Sources: Visa: US merchant surcharge Q&A Mastercard: merchant surcharge rules Mastercard: current registration notice Not legal advice. sources.pageTitle: Do I need to register or give notice before surcharging?
sources.text: Separate notice from customer disclosure Notifying the acquirer is only one step. Visa also requires customer disclosures at entry, at the transaction, and on receipts, plus appropriate transaction-message reporting through the acquirer. Give your provider the launch date and the proposed in-store and online presentation for review. Sources: Visa: US merchant surcharge Q&A

sources.pageTitle: Do I need to register or give notice before surcharging?
sources.text: Resolve the Mastercard documentation difference Mastercard’s general page describes notice to the network and acquirer. Its linked registration page says it is not currently requiring US merchants to register while it revises the rules. Preserve written confirmation from your acquirer rather than treating an old checklist or the unavailable web form as the final answer. Sources: Mastercard: merchant surcharge rules Mastercard: current registration notice Bring your business, not a guess. Talk through your payment setup, website, or next automation. sources.pageTitle: What is the difference between a surcharge and a cash discount?
sources.text: Breadcrumb Home Guides Payment processing What is the difference between a surcharge and a cash discount? KCG field guide · Nationwide What is the difference between a surcharge and a cash discount? A surcharge adds a fee for paying by credit card. A genuine cash discount reduces a displayed regular price for an alternative payment method. Dual pricing shows cash and card prices before payment. The price the customer sees and the amount charged matter more than the program’s marketing name. Free Profit Leak Analysis Book a call By Keystone Consulting Group Last reviewed 2026-10-28 Sources: Visa: US merchant surcharge Q&A Connecticut DCP: surcharges Not legal advice. This is general information from the linked sources, reviewed October 28, 2026. Laws and network rules can change. Have your legal adviser and acquirer review your actual pricing, locations, and checkout before implementation.

sources.pageTitle: What is the difference between a surcharge and a cash discount?
sources.text: Review what the customer sees first Visa permits displaying the card price alone or cash and card prices side by side for a discount offer. If the final card total is reached by adding a fee to the displayed price, Visa says the arrangement may be treated as a surcharge. Changing the receipt label does not resolve the underlying presentation. Sources: Visa: US merchant surcharge Q&A

sources.pageTitle: What is the difference between a surcharge and a cash discount?
sources.text: Keep legal and terminal reviews together A lawful discount arrangement still needs consistent signs, menus, receipts, and online prices. Ask your provider to demonstrate cash, credit, debit, refund, and partial-refund scenarios. Have the legal reviewer approve the presentation before staff begin explaining a new policy to customers. Bring your business, not a guess. Talk through your payment setup, website, or next automation. Free Profit Leak Analysis

sources.pageTitle: What is the difference between a surcharge and a cash discount?

The implementation and applicable rules determine the treatment. Can a receipt fix an undisclosed fee? Do not rely on the receipt alone. Visa requires surcharge disclosures before payment as well as on the receipt, and state price-display rules can add requirements.

sources.pageTitle: How do I switch from Stripe without losing recurring billing?
sources.text: Breadcrumb Home Guides Payment processing How do I switch from Stripe without losing recurring billing? KCG field guide · Nationwide How do I switch from Stripe without losing recurring billing? Treat switching from Stripe as two migrations: payment credentials and billing logic. Stripe can securely transfer eligible card data to a receiving processor, but subscriptions and payment history are not part of that export. Map schedules, balances, retries, and customer permissions separately, then test a controlled cutover before stopping existing billing. Free Profit Leak Analysis Book a call By Keystone Consulting Group Last reviewed 2026-10-28 Sources: Stripe payment data export

sources.pageTitle: How do I switch from Stripe without losing recurring billing?
sources.text: Confirm what can move Stripe’s export documentation excludes credentials saved through Link and does not export subscription objects or payment history in the payment-data transfer. Ask the receiving processor to confirm eligibility and import support first. Do not request raw card data by email or put it in a spreadsheet for manual transfer. Sources: Stripe payment data export

sources.pageTitle: How do I switch from Stripe without losing recurring billing?
sources.text: Rebuild the billing schedule deliberately Create an inventory of customers, next charge dates, prices, credits, trials, tax configuration, cancellations, and failed-payment retries. Assign one system as the authority for each charge during the transition. Reconcile the first cycle against the inventory so a successful import does not conceal missed or duplicate charges. Bring your business, not a guess. Talk through your payment setup, website, or next automation. Free Profit Leak Analysis

sources.pageTitle: How do I switch from Stripe without losing recurring billing?
sources.text: Keep a rollback and access plan Use a test environment and an approved cutover plan before live billing. Stripe says account data remains accessible through the Dashboard and API after processing stops if the account stays open. Decide how long you need that access for historical records and refunds before considering account closure. Sources: Stripe payment data export

sources.pageTitle: How do I switch from Stripe without losing recurring billing?
sources.text: Frequently asked questions Will every saved card transfer? Do not assume that. Stripe excludes Link credentials, and the receiving processor must meet transfer requirements. Identify exceptions before notifying customers. Does transferring cards recreate subscriptions? No. Stripe’s payment-data export does not include subscription objects. Billing schedules need a separate migration plan.

sources.pageTitle: Is zero-fee credit card processing really free?
sources.text: Breadcrumb Home Guides Payment processing Is zero-fee credit card processing really free? KCG field guide · Nationwide Is zero-fee credit card processing really free? No, a zero-fee processing offer does not make card acceptance cost disappear. Cash discount or dual-pricing programs shift that cost to customers through the displayed card price while offering a lower cash price. Ask which processing, gateway, equipment, and software charges remain, and review the price presentation before adopting a program. Free Profit Leak Analysis Book a call By Keystone Consulting Group Last reviewed 2026-11-09 Sources: Visa: US merchant surcharge Q&A Not legal advice. This is general information from the linked sources, reviewed October 28, 2026. Laws and network rules can change. Have your legal adviser and acquirer review your actual pricing, locations, and checkout before implementation.

sources.pageTitle: Is zero-fee credit card processing really free?
sources.text: Check what zero-fee actually covers Ask the provider to explain the offer using your current statement and proposed customer checkout. Identify which costs shift into the customer’s card price. Request all remaining monthly and transaction charges. Separate gateway, equipment, and optional software terms. Review displayed prices and test cash, credit, debit, and refunds.

sources.pageTitle: Is zero-fee credit card processing really free?
sources.text: Understand how customers pay the cost With cash discount or dual pricing, the card price carries costs that a lower cash price avoids. The expense has shifted into pricing; it has not vanished. Ask what the customer sees on a sign, menu, invoice, or website and compare that with the final amount charged. Bring your business, not a guess. Talk through your payment setup, website, or next automation. Free Profit Leak Analysis

sources.pageTitle: Is zero-fee credit card processing really free?
sources.text: Keep discounts and surcharges distinct Visa distinguishes a reduction from a displayed card price from an added fee. A fee added to a posted price may be treated as a surcharge even if the program uses a different name. Read the linked dual-pricing and surcharge guides and have your provider review each location and payment channel. Sources: Visa: US merchant surcharge Q&A

sources.pageTitle: Privacy Policy
sources.text: Privacy Policy Effective September 21, 2026 We take your privacy seriously. Here is how KCG handles your personal and business information.

sources.pageTitle: Privacy Policy
sources.text: What we collect When you contact Keystone Consulting Group LLC (KCG) or book a call, we collect the information you submit: your name, email address, phone number, business information, and any message or notes. Booking also includes the date and time you choose. Only send information we need to help you. Do not put card numbers, passwords, or other sensitive account details in these forms.

sources.pageTitle: Privacy Policy
sources.text: How we use it We use your information to respond to enquiries, understand your business needs, schedule calls, and provide the services you request. We do not sell your personal information.

sources.pageTitle: Privacy Policy
sources.text: Booking and Google Calendar Our booking service uses Google Calendar and Google APIs to check the availability of KCG's calendar and create appointments. We use availability information to offer open times; we do not show visitors the details of other appointments. When you book, your name, email, phone number if provided, and notes are stored in the calendar event on KCG's Google Calendar. Google Calendar emails an invitation to the address you provide. The invitation includes a Google Meet link when one is available. Test bookings marked as dry-run do not create an event or send an invitation.

sources.pageTitle: Privacy Policy
sources.text: Service providers and payment partners Vercel hosts this website and its booking endpoints. Google processes calendar events and their invitations, including meeting information. Our contact and enquiry tools process the information you submit so we can respond. If you ask us to help with payment processing, we may share the business and contact information needed with the payment processing partners KCG works with to evaluate or provide that service. Their applications and services have their own privacy terms. We may also disclose information when required by law.

sources.pageTitle: Privacy Policy
sources.text: Cookies and local storage This site saves your light or dark theme preference in your browser using localStorage under kcg-theme. You can remove it by clearing this site’s browser data. Our hosting and service providers may process technical information such as IP addresses and request logs to deliver and protect their services. Google services you open from an invitation may use cookies under Google’s privacy policy.

sources.pageTitle: Privacy Policy
sources.text: Retention and protection We only retain collected information for as long as necessary to provide your requested service, handle follow-up, and meet applicable recordkeeping obligations. Booking information remains in our Google Calendar until it is no longer needed or we act on a valid deletion request. We limit access to the people and providers who need it to do this work. No website or email system can guarantee absolute security.

sources.pageTitle: Privacy Policy
sources.text: Your choices and requests You can ask to access, correct, or delete the personal information we hold about you by contacting us below. We may need to verify that the request is yours. We will explain if we need to retain a record for a legal obligation or an ongoing service. Removing an event from our calendar does not remove copies of invitations already delivered to an email inbox. You can also contact us to change or cancel a booking.

sources.pageTitle: Privacy Policy
sources.text: SMS / Text Messaging When you opt in to text messages from Keystone Consulting Group LLC (KCG), we collect your mobile phone number, consent and opt-out records, message content, and delivery information to send and manage messages responding to your enquiries or about appointments and services you request. Mobile information, SMS consent, and opt-in data are not sold or shared with third parties or affiliates for their own marketing or promotional purposes. We may share messaging data with service providers only as needed to deliver and support the messaging service, subject to these restrictions. Message frequency varies. Message and data rates may apply. Reply STOP to opt out, reply HELP for help. Consent is not a condition of purchase or service. You can also contact KCG using the contact details below. This SMS section is effective October 5, 2026.

sources.pageTitle: Privacy Policy
sources.text: Changes to this policy We will update this page when our practices change and revise the effective date. Contact us if you need help understanding how this policy applies to your information.

sources.text: All services AI Implementations Hand the repeat work to software that does not forget. Every hour someone spends copying data between tools is an hour nobody spent selling. sources.pageTitle: AI Implementations
sources.text: The work keeps landing back on your desk. A new enquiry arrives while you are serving a customer. By the time someone replies, the prospect has already called elsewhere. The lead was there. The handoff was missing. Your team copies customer details from a message into the CRM, then repeats the entry in another tool. When something changes, someone has to remember every place it was copied. You are interested in AI, but you do not need another dashboard to babysit. You need a specific piece of work to stop landing back on your desk, with a way to see when the software needs help.

sources.pageTitle: AI Implementations
sources.text: AI Lead Qualification We build an agent around the questions your team uses to decide how to handle an enquiry. It collects the relevant details and routes the conversation according to rules you approve. What it replaces Manual sorting of enquiries and repeated introductory questions. It gives your team context before a call instead of making the prospect explain the same thing again. What you get A lead record with the information gathered and a clear next action. Incomplete or ambiguous answers can go to a person for review. Qualification is a routing decision, not proof that someone will buy. Who it is for Businesses with a repeatable enquiry process and a clear definition of a useful lead. If your criteria live only in the owner’s head, we need to make them explicit first.

sources.pageTitle: AI Implementations
sources.text: Customer Service Agents We configure an agent to answer recurring questions from approved business information. You decide what it may handle and which requests must go straight to your staff. What it replaces Repeated replies written from scratch and customers waiting for information that is already documented. Your team keeps the conversations that need judgement or account-specific decisions. What you get Answers grounded in the material you provide, with a handoff when the agent cannot resolve the request. We test uncertain questions as well as easy ones, so an unsupported answer is treated as a failure. Who it is for Teams receiving recurring service questions whose answers can be kept current. If nobody can own the underlying information, the assistant will not stay useful on its own.

sources.pageTitle: AI Implementations
sources.text: Workflow Automation We turn an agreed sequence of routine actions into a workflow. A completed form might create a record and notify its owner. Each action has a defined trigger so you can explain why it happened. What it replaces Copying data between screens and relying on someone to remember the next handoff. We start with a process that already makes sense, then remove the repeated manual steps. What you get A workflow with clear inputs and a visible outcome. We agree what happens when information is missing or a connected tool is unavailable. Your team needs a way to catch exceptions rather than assume every run succeeded. Who it is for Businesses doing the same administrative handoff repeatedly. A process that changes with every case may need human approval at key points instead of automatic execution throughout.

sources.pageTitle: AI Implementations
sources.text: System Integrations We connect the tools you already use where their supported interfaces allow it. We decide which system owns each piece of information and when changes should reach the other system. What it replaces Duplicate entry and conflicting records. A customer update should not become a guessing game about which screen contains the current information. What you get An agreed data handoff between your tools, with field mapping and failure handling checked before use. The scope defines which direction data moves and what must remain under human control. Who it is for Businesses with useful software that does not currently share the information staff need. We inspect access limits first. Paying for a tool does not necessarily mean it permits every integration you want.

sources.pageTitle: AI Implementations
sources.text: What enterprise users reported OpenAI’s enterprise AI report says users reported this much time saved per active day. It is self-reported enterprise experience, not measured savings for KCG clients. It gives us a benchmark to investigate, not an outcome to promise. Derived illustration, assuming use on 5 working days: 40-60 minutes × 5 = 200-300 minutes per week. Divide by 60 minutes per hour = 3 hours 20 minutes to 5 hours per week. This assumes the reported daily saving repeats each day; use your measured saving and actual days instead. Sources: OpenAI, The state of enterprise AI (2025) 14%

sources.pageTitle: AI Implementations
sources.text: Customer support research McKinsey describes a company with 5,000 support agents where generative AI increased issues resolved per hour by 14%. This concerns support work in that setting. It does not establish the same improvement for your team or mean staff can be removed. Derived: baseline issues resolved per hour × (1 + 14 / 100) = baseline × 1.14. This expresses the study’s productivity change; it is not a 14% reduction in working hours. Sources: McKinsey, The promise and the reality of gen AI agents in the enterprise (May 2024)

sources.pageTitle: AI Implementations
sources.text: Discovery: watch the work happen Walk Seth and Hunter through a real enquiry or repeated task. We identify where people wait and where information gets copied. We agree a baseline and choose a bounded workflow, including the cases that should stay with a person.

sources.pageTitle: AI Implementations
sources.text: Build: test the rules against real cases We configure the agent or workflow around your approved process. You review its answers and routing decisions. We test missing information and failed connections as well as the expected path before giving it a live responsibility.

sources.pageTitle: AI Implementations
sources.text: Launch: introduce it with oversight We agree what can run automatically and what needs approval. Your team checks early results against the original task. A fast reply that sends a lead to the wrong place is a defect, even if the automation ran successfully.

sources.pageTitle: AI Implementations
sources.text: Handover: give someone ownership We train the people who will use the workflow and agree who maintains its business information. You see how to handle exceptions and when to pause it. Any ongoing support arrangement and software fees are specified in the scope.

sources.pageTitle: AI Implementations
sources.text: A good fit You can point to recurring work and show how the team handles it today. Someone can approve the answers and own changes to the process. Your existing tools permit the access needed for the agreed workflow.

sources.pageTitle: AI Implementations
sources.text: Not a good fit You want AI to make every judgement without anyone reviewing exceptions. Your process changes constantly and nobody can define a reliable handoff. You expect a guaranteed headcount reduction or savings figure before measuring the work.

sources.pageTitle: AI Implementations
sources.text: What does an AI implementation cost? The quote depends on the workflow and the systems it touches. We separate build work from recurring software or usage fees. KCG looks for processing savings first, then discusses reinvesting verified savings. We do not assume those savings will pay for everything.

sources.pageTitle: AI Implementations
sources.text: How long until it works? We agree a schedule after checking access and the process itself. A workflow is ready when it handles the agreed cases and exceptions reliably enough for its role. Measurable value takes actual use and a comparison with the baseline, not a launch announcement.

sources.pageTitle: AI Implementations
sources.text: Do we need to replace our CRM or website? Usually the first step is to inspect what you already have. We build around your actual workflow and check what your tools allow. If a connection is unavailable or would require a different subscription, we explain that before including it in the scope.

sources.pageTitle: AI Implementations
sources.text: What happens when the AI gets something wrong? We define where it must ask for help and how staff review its output. An agent should not invent an answer because the business information is missing. The launch checks include unclear requests, and your team needs a clear way to take over.

sources.pageTitle: AI Implementations
sources.text: Do we own the implementation? Ownership and access are written into the scope for the work we build. Third-party models and tools retain their own licenses and fees. If a website is part of the project, you own that site. We explain dependencies before you commit.

sources.pageTitle: AI Implementations
sources.text: How much time will we actually get back? We measure the task before and after, including the time spent correcting output or handling exceptions. That gives you a daily figure measured against your own baseline, not a projection. Recovered time can create room for other work; it is not automatically money removed from payroll.

sources.pageTitle: AI Implementations
sources.text: What do you need from our team? Examples of the work and an owner who can say what a correct result looks like. We identify the account access required for the agreed connections. You approve the information an agent may use and the actions it may take before it handles live work.

sources.pageTitle: AI Implementations
sources.text: Show us the task you keep repeating. Describe the handoff that keeps coming back to your desk and the tools involved. Seth or Hunter will review where automation fits and what needs to stay with your people.

When nobody can answer or follow up, that opportunity may disappear before you finish the job in front of you. We arrange business process outsourcing for inbound lead handling, appointment setting and quote follow-up, with clear rules for what the person answering can promise. On this page What we build What is included The numbers The build process Common questions

sources.pageTitle: BPO Services
sources.text: The work keeps landing back on your desk. This is for owners who are on the tools, reception teams stretched at busy times, and businesses whose enquiries sit untouched. Trades, clinics, salons and dealers need coverage that fits their actual opening hours and workload. The purpose is to make existing demand easier to handle, not to manufacture a calendar full of buyers.

sources.pageTitle: BPO Services
sources.text: Answer with enough context to help Give callers a useful response when your own staff are occupied. We define the questions reception can answer and the details to collect. Coverage hours and escalation contacts are agreed first, so an urgent request does not sit in the same queue as a routine enquiry.

sources.pageTitle: BPO Services
sources.text: Send the right enquiries to your team Spend less time reconstructing why someone called. We use approved qualification questions about the request, location and timing, then record the answers in the agreed system. A qualified lead meets your routing criteria; it is not a guarantee that the customer will buy.

sources.pageTitle: BPO Services
sources.text: Book appointments your staff can deliver Reduce the back-and-forth around availability. We define appointment types and booking rules, including travel or preparation time where relevant. Your team receives the customer's context before the visit. Requests outside those rules go to a named person instead of being forced into the calendar.

sources.pageTitle: BPO Services
sources.text: Give outstanding quotes a next step Find out whether a customer needs clarification, wants to proceed or has chosen someone else. Follow-up uses your approved wording and respects a request to stop. Responses update the pipeline, so staff can act on real interest instead of repeatedly calling the same unresolved list.

sources.pageTitle: BPO Services
sources.text: Know what happened to each enquiry See handling activity and outcomes in a report you can inspect. We track agreed measures such as response time and attended appointments, with missed handoffs made visible. Reviewing the records helps distinguish a coverage problem from weak demand or a service your business cannot provide.

sources.pageTitle: BPO Services
sources.text: What a KCG build includes The scope sets coverage, volume assumptions and the handoff. Staff availability and service commitments must be confirmed before launch. A handling playbook Approved answers and qualification questions, plus requests that must go directly to your team. A booking and handoff setup Agreed calendar access, CRM fields and notification paths, tested with sample enquiries before real work begins. A quote follow-up routine A defined list, contact schedule and stop conditions. Your staff handle negotiation or technical advice outside the script. A review and coverage agreement Reporting responsibilities and a named escalation contact. Charges for extra volume or extended hours are made explicit.

sources.pageTitle: BPO Services
sources.text: Put a number on the time bought back Published research gives us a reason to measure. Your own results determine what the work is worth. 21x

sources.pageTitle: BPO Services
sources.text: A reason to make response time visible MIT/InsideSales research reported 21 times higher qualification odds when web leads were called within five minutes rather than thirty. This older finding does not establish an answer rate for inbound calls or guarantee appointments. Sources: MIT/InsideSales, Lead Response Management study (2007); InsideSales recap (2015) 56%

sources.pageTitle: BPO Services
sources.text: Coverage still has to make financial sense The Federal Reserve reported 60% of firms sought financing; among financing seekers, 56% cited operating expenses. This gives cost-pressure context, not evidence that outsourcing is always cheaper. Sources: Federal Reserve, 2026 Report on Employer Firms (2025 survey)

sources.pageTitle: BPO Services
sources.text: Map: follow the inbound path We review how enquiries arrive and where they wait. You choose the coverage gap to address and define which calls need your immediate attention.

sources.pageTitle: BPO Services
sources.text: Prepare: approve the handling rules We write the playbook and confirm access. Sample calls test booking limits and escalation before anyone makes promises on behalf of your business.

sources.pageTitle: BPO Services
sources.text: Launch: inspect early handoffs We start within the agreed coverage and review records with your team. Incorrect bookings or missing information lead to changes in the handling process.

sources.pageTitle: BPO Services
sources.text: Review: compare cost and usefulness We examine response and appointment outcomes alongside the service bill. Volume changes may call for different coverage or for improving the underlying sales process.

sources.pageTitle: BPO Services
sources.text: A good fit You receive enquiries but cannot consistently answer or follow up. You can supply approved answers and a reliable staff escalation contact.

sources.pageTitle: BPO Services
sources.text: Not a good fit You need clinical, technical or pricing decisions made without qualified staff. You expect guaranteed sales from every booked appointment.

sources.pageTitle: BPO Services
sources.text: Is this a cold-calling campaign? This service focuses on inbound enquiries, reception and follow-up on existing interest. New outbound prospecting needs a separate scope and should not be confused with answering demand you already have.

sources.pageTitle: BPO Services
sources.text: Can you cover evenings and weekends? We discuss the hours and likely volume first, then confirm what coverage is available and what it costs. Do not assume continuous coverage from the service name.

sources.pageTitle: BPO Services
sources.text: Will callers get accurate answers? The team works from your approved information and sends unfamiliar questions to you. Someone inside your business must keep that information current when services or availability change.

sources.pageTitle: BPO Services
sources.text: Is outsourcing cheaper than hiring? Sometimes, but it depends on volume and coverage. We compare the actual service cost with your staffing options, including the time needed to supervise either arrangement.

sources.pageTitle: BPO Services
sources.text: How do we judge whether it works? Track meaningful contacts and attended appointments against the starting point. Arithmetic: unanswered paid enquiries still carry their acquisition cost. Recovered enquiries only add value when the follow-through is useful.

sources.pageTitle: BPO Services
sources.text: Show us where enquiries stop moving. Bring a sample of missed calls or outstanding quotes and your busiest hours. Seth or Hunter will discuss the coverage and handoff needed to keep them moving.

sources.text: All services Business Loans Match the funding to the work it needs to do. Steady demand does not always arrive with the cash needed to fulfil it. We help you assess working capital or funding for equipment and expansion, match the request to suitable products, and organise the paperwork. The right money should support the business through repayment. Clearing an immediate cash shortage is only the start. On this page What we build What is included The numbers The build process Common questions

sources.pageTitle: Business Loans
sources.text: The work keeps landing back on your desk. This is for businesses held back by cash timing, a necessary equipment purchase or growth that needs funding before it produces revenue. If an earlier application returned only part of what you needed, we review the gap and the repayment capacity. A larger loan is useful only if the business can carry it.

sources.pageTitle: Business Loans
sources.text: Bridge a defined operating gap Keep an identified cash shortfall from interrupting work you can deliver profitably. We review when customer payments arrive against upcoming expenses and discuss working-capital options. Borrowing to cover a timing gap is different from borrowing to support continuing losses; the second problem needs a wider operating review.

sources.pageTitle: Business Loans
sources.text: Buy equipment without guessing at affordability Assess the cost of adding or replacing equipment alongside its expected use. We help organise the purchase details and compare available funding structures. The repayment period should make sense for the asset and business, with deposits and any security requirements understood before you commit.

sources.pageTitle: Business Loans
sources.text: Fund growth on a realistic schedule Make an expansion plan account for the wait before new revenue arrives. We review the amount needed and discuss suitable term or other available products. Forecasts include the slower case, because a new location or service can take longer to contribute than the sales plan assumes.

sources.pageTitle: Business Loans
sources.text: Compare offers beyond the headline payment Know what an offer asks of the business. We organise the information needed to compare proceeds received, total repayment and payment frequency, alongside fees and security terms. A factor rate is not an annual percentage rate. We identify unclear terms for the provider to explain in writing.

sources.pageTitle: Business Loans
sources.text: Present a complete funding request Reduce avoidable back-and-forth by preparing the documents the provider requests. We help explain the use of funds and keep missing items visible. Accurate records improve the application process; they do not override underwriting or turn a previous decline into a promised approval.

sources.pageTitle: Business Loans
sources.text: What a KCG build includes The engagement defines application support and available provider options. You review any fees and authorise submissions before they are made. A funding-needs review The purpose, requested amount and timing, checked against current cash flow and existing repayment commitments. A product comparison Options suited to the request, with total costs and repayment structure reviewed rather than relying on a headline rate. A document checklist Required records and a clear list of missing information. Your accountant supplies or confirms financial statements where needed. An offer and funding handoff Support reviewing provider questions and funding conditions. The lender makes the credit decision and controls disbursement.

sources.pageTitle: Business Loans
sources.text: Put a number on the time bought back Published research gives us a reason to measure. Your own results determine what the work is worth. 42% / 36% / 22%

sources.pageTitle: Business Loans
sources.text: Many applicants receive less than requested Among financing applicants, 42% received the full amount, 36% some or most, and 22% none. These are employer-firm outcomes, not approval odds for your application. Sources: Federal Reserve, 2026 Report on Employer Firms (2025 survey) 60%

sources.pageTitle: Business Loans
sources.text: Funding often supports day-to-day operations 60% of firms applied for financing in the prior year. Operating expenses were cited by 56% of financing seekers; expansion or a new opportunity by 46%. Sources: Federal Reserve, 2026 Report on Employer Firms (2025 survey) 57%

sources.pageTitle: Business Loans
sources.text: The provider matters Applicants at small banks were most likely to receive full approval, at 57%. Different applicant groups mean this is not proof a particular bank will approve you. Sources: Federal Reserve, 2026 Report on Employer Firms (2025 survey)

sources.pageTitle: Business Loans
sources.text: Review: define the funding job We establish the use of funds and timing, then review repayment capacity. An application needs a reason for the amount beyond borrowing the maximum available.

sources.pageTitle: Business Loans
sources.text: Prepare: organise the evidence We compile the requested documents and flag gaps. You verify the business information and approve where an application will be submitted.

sources.pageTitle: Business Loans
sources.text: Compare: understand the offer We review written terms and questions for the provider. You consider total cost and the effect of payments during a slower trading period.

sources.pageTitle: Business Loans
sources.text: Complete: confirm the conditions We help track outstanding requirements and confirm the provider's next steps. You rely on written funding confirmation before committing money you have not received.

sources.pageTitle: Business Loans
sources.text: A good fit You have steady revenue and a clear use for additional capital. You can document cash flow and assess repayment alongside existing debt.

sources.pageTitle: Business Loans
sources.text: Not a good fit You want guaranteed funding or a fixed approval time before underwriting. You need borrowing to hide a recurring loss with no credible repayment plan.

sources.pageTitle: Business Loans
sources.text: Can you guarantee an approval? No. Providers assess the business and decide what to offer. We help prepare the request and explain options; a complete application can still be declined.

sources.pageTitle: Business Loans
sources.text: How quickly can funds arrive? It depends on the product and funding conditions, including any documents still needed. We confirm the provider's timetable for your case rather than advertise a blanket turnaround.

sources.pageTitle: Business Loans
sources.text: Can you help after a bank decline? We can review the stated reason and whether a different product fits. More expensive money is not automatically a solution, particularly if repayment capacity caused the decline.

sources.pageTitle: Business Loans
sources.text: Will I need a personal guarantee? Some products require one or other security. We identify the requirement in the offer so you can assess the obligation before signing, with professional advice where needed.

sources.pageTitle: Business Loans
sources.text: What will this cost? The written offer and engagement terms should show lender charges and any KCG or referral compensation. We review total repayment and actual proceeds; we do not promise a fee-free application.

sources.pageTitle: Business Loans
sources.text: Bring the funding gap and the numbers behind it. Tell Seth or Hunter what the capital would pay for and when revenue should follow. We will discuss the records needed to assess suitable funding options.

sources.pageTitle: Consulting Services
sources.text: All services Consulting Services Know what to fix first, and who will get it done. You can have customers, capable staff and a full calendar while every decision still comes back to you. We find where time and money leak, choose the changes worth making, and put them in an order your team can deliver. Advisory work should end in decisions you can act on. On this page What we build What is included The numbers The build process Common questions

sources.pageTitle: Consulting Services
sources.text: The work keeps landing back on your desk. This is for owners with a business worth growing but no room left to manage another initiative. Perhaps you bought tools that never stuck. Perhaps the same problem returns every month. We start with how work actually happens, because buying another system before understanding the problem can make it more expensive.

sources.pageTitle: Consulting Services
sources.text: Find the cost behind the frustration See which problems deserve attention before spending on a fix. We review recurring costs and follow a sample of work from enquiry to payment. A subscription charge is easy to spot; duplicated effort and quotes left unanswered need a closer look at the process.

sources.pageTitle: Consulting Services
sources.text: Choose changes your team can use Get a recommendation tied to a specific business need. We compare improving the current process with configuring existing software or building something new. AI is considered where it fits. A basic checklist can be the better answer when judgement and ownership are the missing pieces.

sources.pageTitle: Consulting Services
sources.text: Put the work in a sensible order Avoid launching changes that depend on unfinished groundwork. We identify access requirements and staff time, then sequence the work around daily operations. Each recommendation has an owner and a way to judge whether it helped, so the plan can survive a busy week.

sources.pageTitle: Consulting Services
sources.text: Keep decisions moving after the meeting Get regular reviews of what changed and what is still stuck. We challenge assumptions against the agreed baseline and adjust the next action. If implementation is included, its scope is written down; an advisory meeting alone does not mean software or staff training has been delivered.

sources.pageTitle: Consulting Services
sources.text: What a KCG build includes You receive a practical decision record and delivery plan. The engagement defines which areas we inspect and how often we meet. An operating baseline A record of current costs and the work being reviewed, with estimates clearly distinguished from verified amounts. A prioritised action plan Recommended changes with expected benefits and an accountable owner. Dependencies are documented. Unproven ideas stay marked as assumptions. A tool and implementation brief Requirements you can use to compare options, including recurring costs and the time your team must contribute. A review cadence Scheduled check-ins and a short progress record. Implementation work and specialist accounting or legal advice are scoped separately.

sources.pageTitle: Consulting Services
sources.text: Put a number on the time bought back Published research gives us a reason to measure. Your own results determine what the work is worth. 46% + 15%

sources.pageTitle: Consulting Services
sources.text: Interest is already there In the Federal Reserve's 2025 employer-firm survey, 46% used AI and another 15% planned to start within a year. Sources: Federal Reserve, 2026 Report on Employer Firms (2025 survey) 54%

sources.pageTitle: Consulting Services
sources.text: Choosing the right tool is a barrier Among planned AI adopters, 54% cited finding tools that meet business needs as a challenge. Sources: Federal Reserve, 2026 Report on Employer Firms (2025 survey) 37%

sources.pageTitle: Consulting Services
sources.text: Making time is another barrier Among those planned adopters, 37% cited implementation or employee-training time. Our interpretation: selection and delivery deserve as much attention as willingness to adopt. Sources: Federal Reserve, 2026 Report on Employer Firms (2025 survey)

sources.pageTitle: Consulting Services
sources.text: Review: see the work We speak with the owner and staff doing the work, then inspect agreed records. We separate a recurring problem from an isolated bad week.

sources.pageTitle: Consulting Services
sources.text: Decide: rank the fixes You review the evidence and choose the first priority. We record the tradeoffs and the work that should wait until prerequisites are finished.

sources.pageTitle: Consulting Services
sources.text: Implement: assign responsibility Each action gets an owner and an agreed checkpoint. We support delivery within scope and raise blockers before they become another abandoned project.

sources.pageTitle: Consulting Services
sources.text: Measure: decide what comes next We compare results with the baseline, including staff effort and ongoing fees. You decide whether to continue, change course or stop an initiative.

sources.pageTitle: Consulting Services
sources.text: A good fit You are growing but remain the approval point for routine work. You can share operating records and give staff time to change a process.

sources.pageTitle: Consulting Services
sources.text: Not a good fit You want a presentation with no decisions or follow-through. You have already chosen a tool and only want someone to endorse it.

sources.pageTitle: Consulting Services
sources.text: Is this only about AI? No. We look at the business problem first. The answer might involve payments, a CRM, clearer responsibilities or removing an unnecessary step from an existing process.

sources.pageTitle: Consulting Services
sources.text: Will you implement the recommendations? We can scope delivery separately or alongside the review. You will know which changes KCG owns and which require your team or another provider.

sources.pageTitle: Consulting Services
sources.text: What if we already tried consulting? Bring the old recommendations and what happened afterward. We look for missing ownership, unrealistic dependencies or a mismatch with daily work before proposing another plan.

sources.pageTitle: Consulting Services
sources.text: How much of my time will this take? We agree meeting time and access needs before starting. Someone inside the business must approve decisions and make staff available; we cannot discover every constraint from a spreadsheet.

sources.pageTitle: Consulting Services
sources.text: How do we know it paid off? We agree what to measure before the change. Reduced repeat work, lower verified costs or faster quote handling can be useful measures. Advice is not a guaranteed profit increase.

sources.pageTitle: Consulting Services
sources.text: Bring the problem that keeps returning. Tell Seth or Hunter what you have tried and where work still lands on your desk. We will discuss a bounded review and the evidence needed to choose your first fix.

sources.text: All services Consumer Financing Give customers a clear way to spread a larger purchase. A customer can want the work and still be unable to pay the whole invoice today. We help you evaluate pay-over-time options and fit an application flow into quoting or checkout. Customers see the available terms, and your staff understand what approval and funding actually mean before promising a start date. On this page What we build What is included The numbers The build process Common questions

sources.pageTitle: Consumer Financing
sources.text: The work keeps landing back on your desk. This is for businesses selling larger jobs or purchases: HVAC, roofing, remodels, dental, auto repair, equipment and higher-ticket retail. Payment timing can be the obstacle even after a customer understands the value. Financing offers another route to purchase, provided the customer qualifies and the cost works for both sides.

sources.pageTitle: Consumer Financing
sources.text: Discuss payment options before the sale stalls Let customers consider an eligible plan while reviewing the quote. We help place the application step where staff can explain it without pressuring the customer. The full purchase price stays clear alongside any monthly illustration and lender-provided terms. A smaller payment does not mean a cheaper purchase.

sources.pageTitle: Consumer Financing
sources.text: Match the program to what you sell Avoid offering a product that does not support your industry or typical job size. We compare available programs against those requirements and review merchant charges. Approval criteria and customer pricing belong to the provider; we do not promise that every applicant will qualify.

sources.pageTitle: Consumer Financing
sources.text: Know when you can expect payment Plan fulfilment around the actual funding conditions. We review when the provider releases funds and whether completion evidence or other steps are required. Staff should distinguish an application, an approval and a funded transaction. The applicable agreement determines settlement timing and merchant responsibilities.

sources.pageTitle: Consumer Financing
sources.text: Fit the process into your payment setup Keep applications and invoices from becoming disconnected. We scope the supported checkout, payment link or in-person flow, then define who checks status. Where a direct connection is unavailable, the written handoff tells staff what to verify before recording the sale as paid.

sources.pageTitle: Consumer Financing
sources.text: What a KCG build includes The project is a program review and implementation of the agreed flow. Lender approval and merchant onboarding are separate requirements. A program comparison Available options assessed against your industry and sale size, with fees, settlement conditions and dependencies identified. An application path A tested route from the quote or checkout to the provider's application, using its approved disclosures and materials. A staff operating guide How to introduce the option, check status and handle a declined application without promising approval elsewhere. A funding and refund handoff Who confirms settlement and who contacts the provider when a job changes or is cancelled. Ongoing provider costs stay visible.

sources.pageTitle: Consumer Financing
sources.text: Put a number on the time bought back Published research gives us a reason to measure. Your own results determine what the work is worth. 93%

sources.pageTitle: Consumer Financing
sources.text: Reviews inform purchase decisions BrightLocal's 2026 survey found 93% had bought after reading reviews. This supports showing credible business information alongside payment options; it does not measure financing results. Sources: BrightLocal, Local Consumer Review Survey (2026) 27%

sources.pageTitle: Consumer Financing
sources.text: Some reviewed purchases are substantial BrightLocal found 27% had spent more than $1,000 after reading reviews. That is purchase context, not evidence of financing-driven sales growth. Sources: BrightLocal, Local Consumer Review Survey (2026)

sources.pageTitle: Consumer Financing
sources.text: Review: understand your sales We discuss typical invoices and when payment objections arise. You provide the payment setup and the timing needed to order materials or begin work.

sources.pageTitle: Consumer Financing
sources.text: Compare: inspect the terms We review program eligibility and merchant costs. You decide whether the available options suit your margins before committing to onboarding or integration work.

sources.pageTitle: Consumer Financing
sources.text: Implement: test the customer path We configure the agreed application handoff and train staff to use approved explanations. The checks cover declines and incomplete applications as well as the expected flow.

sources.pageTitle: Consumer Financing
sources.text: Handover: measure actual use We agree how to review applications, funded sales and fees. Your own data can show whether the program helps; we do not substitute a vendor's sales-lift claim.

sources.pageTitle: Consumer Financing
sources.text: A good fit Customers want larger purchases but sometimes need to spread payment. You have enough margin to evaluate provider fees and clear fulfilment rules.

sources.pageTitle: Consumer Financing
sources.text: Not a good fit You want guaranteed approvals or a guaranteed increase in order value. You need payment before the provider allows funding and cannot carry that gap.

sources.pageTitle: Consumer Financing
sources.text: Will this increase our close rate? It may help customers whose obstacle is payment timing, but we cannot promise a percentage. We measure completed, funded sales and the costs against your own starting point.

sources.pageTitle: Consumer Financing
sources.text: Do we receive the full price upfront? The provider's agreement controls timing and deductions. Merchant fees, completion requirements or reserves may apply. We review those details before you plan cash flow around a financed sale.

sources.pageTitle: Consumer Financing
sources.text: Is there any risk left with us? Yes, there can be obligations for refunds, disputes, fraud or contract breaches. Lender underwriting does not remove your responsibility to deliver the agreed goods or work.

sources.pageTitle: Consumer Financing
sources.text: What happens if a customer is declined? Staff should explain that the provider made the decision and offer any other payment methods you accept. A different plan may have different criteria, but another approval is never assumed.

sources.pageTitle: Consumer Financing
sources.text: Can we advertise a monthly payment? Use the provider's approved illustrations and required terms. The amount depends on the actual price, repayment period and financing cost. We avoid unsupported examples that make borrowing look free.

sources.pageTitle: Consumer Financing
sources.text: Why offer this instead of discounting? Arithmetic: a sale that cannot proceed under payment-in-full terms contributes no sale revenue today. A funded plan may allow it to proceed, less fees and fulfilment costs. That comparison is not a study finding or a prediction that every declined quote becomes a sale.

sources.pageTitle: Consumer Financing
sources.text: Check whether financing fits your larger jobs. Bring a typical invoice, your margins and when you need payment. Seth or Hunter will discuss available program requirements and the cost of adding pay-over-time.
