sources.pageTitle: CRM Systems
sources.text: The work keeps landing back on your desk. If two or more people sell or quote, a missed handoff can leave a good prospect waiting. Trades with outstanding estimates feel this every week. So do teams whose Monday meeting exists mainly to find out where deals stand. The follow-up that never happens is money you never get the chance to earn.

sources.pageTitle: CRM Systems
sources.text: See every deal and its next action Know which quotes need attention without asking everyone for an update. We map stages to real decisions, give each opportunity an owner, and show the next action with a due date. A stalled quote stays visible until someone resolves it.

sources.pageTitle: CRM Systems
sources.text: Get value from the software you own Keep a platform that fits and fix the setup around it. We review unused fields, confusing stages and duplicate records in your existing CRM. If your workflow needs a custom system, we explain the maintenance and ownership tradeoffs before recommending a build.

sources.pageTitle: CRM Systems
sources.text: Follow up while interest is still there Give staff a prompt when an enquiry arrives or a quote needs a reply. We configure assignments and agreed messages, with stop rules when someone responds or opts out. An automatic acknowledgement supports the handoff; it does not replace a useful conversation.

sources.pageTitle: CRM Systems
sources.text: Run the meeting from reliable numbers See open value, ageing opportunities and closed business from the same records your team works in. We agree what each report means before building it. Forecasts remain estimates, and missing data stays visible instead of making the month look healthier than it is.

sources.pageTitle: CRM Systems
sources.text: What a KCG build includes The scope names the workflow and records included, along with each connection. Training is part of making the system usable. A pipeline your team recognises Defined stages, required fields and ownership rules, reviewed with the people who actually sell. A controlled data move An agreed import, duplicate review and spot checks against your old records. Historic notes are included where the source permits export. Working follow-up and reporting Tested reminders and scoped integrations, plus dashboards with clear definitions and an exception queue. Access and handover Staff permissions, practical training and written support arrangements. Platform subscriptions and later changes are priced separately.

sources.pageTitle: CRM Systems
sources.text: Put a number on the time bought back Published research gives us a reason to measure. Your own results determine what the work is worth. $3.10

sources.pageTitle: CRM Systems
sources.text: Return depends on execution Nucleus Research reported this average return per dollar spent in its 2024 analysis, alongside a 37% decline over the preceding ten years. That does not prove why returns fell. Our takeaway: measure workflow improvements instead of assuming a software purchase creates value. Sources: Nucleus Research, CRM benefit areas with the greatest ROI impact (2024) 21x

sources.pageTitle: CRM Systems
sources.text: Speed gives follow-up a purpose The MIT/InsideSales lead-response research reported 21 times higher qualification odds for web leads called within five minutes versus thirty. This older finding concerns qualification, not closed sales or a promised return from your CRM. Sources: MIT/InsideSales, Lead Response Management study (2007); InsideSales recap (2015)

sources.pageTitle: CRM Systems
sources.text: Discovery: follow a real quote We trace an enquiry through your current process and identify where ownership disappears. You choose a staff member to approve the new workflow.

sources.pageTitle: CRM Systems
sources.text: Configure: keep the useful parts We build or configure the agreed stages, import a sample and test the rules. Your team checks that the system reflects the work.

sources.pageTitle: CRM Systems
sources.text: Launch: work real opportunities Staff use the pipeline with oversight. We check assignments and follow-up delivery, including replied-to leads that should leave an automated sequence.

sources.pageTitle: CRM Systems
sources.text: Handover: keep it current We train the process owner and agree how to review overdue work. Ongoing support and software costs are documented before handover.

sources.pageTitle: CRM Systems
sources.text: A good fit You have multiple people selling or quoting and need shared customer history. You can name someone to keep stages and records accurate.

sources.pageTitle: CRM Systems
sources.text: Not a good fit You expect software to fix a sales process nobody will follow. You need a guaranteed revenue increase before measuring your current pipeline.

sources.pageTitle: CRM Systems
sources.text: Do we have to replace our CRM? No. We inspect the current setup first. A cleaner pipeline and better handoffs may solve the problem without a migration or another subscription.

sources.pageTitle: CRM Systems
sources.text: Will my team actually use it? We involve the people entering the data and remove fields without a purpose. Adoption still needs an owner who uses the same system and follows up on missing records.

sources.pageTitle: CRM Systems
sources.text: Can you bring our old data across? We check export access and sample records before agreeing the migration. Unsupported attachments or incomplete history are identified before you rely on the new system.

sources.pageTitle: CRM Systems
sources.text: What does it cost? Cost depends on configuration, migration and connections. The quote separates implementation from platform fees and support so you can judge the full commitment.

sources.pageTitle: CRM Systems
sources.text: Can it text leads automatically? Where the platform supports it, yes. We agree permission handling, message content and stop rules. Staff retain control when a customer needs a real answer.

sources.pageTitle: CRM Systems
sources.text: Show us the quotes nobody has followed up. Bring your current pipeline, even if it is a spreadsheet. Seth or Hunter will map the next actions and discuss whether your existing CRM can handle them.

sources.pageTitle: Google My Business Profile
sources.text: The work keeps landing back on your desk. Trades, clinics, salons, restaurants, dealerships and professional services all need a credible local presence. A profile is free to create, which makes getting the basics right a useful place to start. The ongoing job is keeping it current when the owner is busy serving the very customers who could leave a review.

sources.pageTitle: Google My Business Profile
sources.text: Make the first impression accurate Help customers reach the right business with the right expectations. We review account access and appropriate categories. Services, opening hours and contact details are checked for accuracy. Service areas reflect where you actually work. Eligibility and verification are checked before setup; Google controls its approval process.

sources.pageTitle: Google My Business Profile
sources.text: Show customers what they will find Make your profile useful with current photographs and clear descriptions. We organise images of your actual premises, work or team, using material you have permission to publish. Posts communicate relevant updates and offers. Posting frequently is not a promise of better rankings.

sources.pageTitle: Google My Business Profile
sources.text: Make review requests part of the work Give customers an easy route to leave honest feedback after a completed visit or job. We agree when to ask and who owns the request. The flow should reach customers consistently, without buying reviews or directing only satisfied people to the public review page.

sources.pageTitle: Google My Business Profile
sources.text: Reply like someone is listening Show the next reader how you handle feedback. We establish a response routine and escalation path for complaints, with replies specific to the experience. Private customer details stay out of public responses. A draft can save time, but someone still needs to check what happened.

sources.pageTitle: Google My Business Profile
sources.text: Carry interest through to an enquiry Connect profile links to a useful service, booking or contact page. We check that the destination works on a phone and matches the offer. If your website leaves visitors unsure what to do, we can scope Website Design work alongside the profile improvements.

sources.pageTitle: Google My Business Profile
sources.text: What a KCG build includes Setup and ongoing care are separate responsibilities. Your scope states who updates the profile after the initial work. An access and accuracy review Ownership checks and a record of missing or conflicting business information. You retain control of the business account. A completed profile within scope Relevant categories and services, current hours and approved photos, with verification dependencies identified. A review and response routine Request wording, a review link and an agreed owner for replies. Sensitive or disputed feedback goes to you. A maintenance handover Instructions for changing hours and publishing updates, plus agreed reporting. Continued management is quoted separately.

sources.pageTitle: Google My Business Profile
sources.text: Put a number on the time bought back Published research gives us a reason to measure. Your own results determine what the work is worth. 47%

sources.pageTitle: Google My Business Profile
sources.text: A small review count can exclude you BrightLocal found 47% would not use a business with fewer than twenty reviews. Its 2026 survey also found 97% read local-business reviews. Sources: BrightLocal, Local Consumer Review Survey (2026) 68%

sources.pageTitle: Google My Business Profile
sources.text: Expectations are getting tougher BrightLocal found 68% required at least four stars, up from 55% the previous year. These are stated consumer preferences, not guaranteed booking rates. Sources: BrightLocal, Local Consumer Review Survey (2026) 89%

sources.pageTitle: Google My Business Profile
sources.text: Replies are part of the service BrightLocal found 89% expected a response to their review; 81% expected it within a week. A review routine needs time for replies. Sources: BrightLocal, Local Consumer Review Survey (2026) 54%

sources.pageTitle: Google My Business Profile
sources.text: Your website still has a job BrightLocal found 54% visited a business website after positive reviews. The profile and website need to make the same next step clear. Sources: BrightLocal, Local Consumer Review Survey (2026)

sources.pageTitle: Google My Business Profile
sources.text: Review: inspect the local presence We check profile access and compare the public information with how you operate. You confirm locations, hours and the services customers should see.

sources.pageTitle: Google My Business Profile
sources.text: Complete: correct the essentials We prepare the agreed edits and help with the verification steps Google requests. Ownership disputes or suspensions may require a separate resolution process.

sources.pageTitle: Google My Business Profile
sources.text: Activate: start the review routine Your team tests the request link and approves response responsibilities. We check the website or booking handoff before relying on it for enquiries.

sources.pageTitle: Google My Business Profile
sources.text: Maintain: keep information useful We agree who handles changed hours, new photos and review replies. Reporting follows the measures available rather than inventing a direct link from every view to a sale.

sources.pageTitle: Google My Business Profile
sources.text: A good fit You serve customers at an eligible location or within a local service area. You can provide accurate information and assign someone to handle feedback.

sources.pageTitle: Google My Business Profile
sources.text: Not a good fit You want invented reviews, a fake location or a guaranteed map position. You expect a one-time setup to keep hours and customer feedback current forever.

sources.pageTitle: Google My Business Profile
sources.text: Is Google My Business the same thing? Yes. Google Business Profile is the current name for the listing customers use in Search and Maps.

sources.pageTitle: Google My Business Profile
sources.text: Can you recover a profile someone else controls? We can review the ownership situation and help with Google's access process. Recovery depends on the account history and evidence; we cannot promise an approval date.

sources.pageTitle: Google My Business Profile
sources.text: Can you remove a negative review? We can flag content that appears to violate platform policy. A negative opinion alone is not grounds for removal. We help you respond clearly and take the underlying issue offline.

sources.pageTitle: Google My Business Profile
sources.text: Do we need a website as well? A profile can generate contact on its own. A useful website gives people space to inspect services and request a quote when the profile does not answer enough.

sources.pageTitle: Google My Business Profile
sources.text: What are we paying for if the profile is free? You pay for the agreed setup and management work. Google does not charge for the profile itself. Photo production, website work or ongoing care need their own scope.

sources.pageTitle: Google My Business Profile
sources.text: See what nearby customers see first. Send your profile link and the area you serve. Seth or Hunter will review missing information, the review routine and the path from your listing to an enquiry.

sources.pageTitle: Grok Bot for Role-Based Work in Your Tools
sources.text: Breadcrumb Services Virtual assistants Grok Bot xAI Role-based assistant on signed-in tools Grok Bot for Role-Based Work in Your Tools A named Bot for a named job, signed into the tools that job needs, with review before sensitive actions. Grok Bot is a role-based AI teammate with its own computer. You give it a job such as sales follow-up, customer service, scheduling, or ops, sign it into the tools that job needs, teach the repeatable steps, and keep sensitive actions behind review. Slack can be one place the team talks to it. It is not the product.

sources.pageTitle: Grok Bot for Role-Based Work in Your Tools
sources.text: Owner requests this job can take Plain requests an owner would actually say. The assistant prepares. A named human decides. Sales Bot: find the last email with the approved quote and show me the original. Draft the follow-up in my voice from approved samples, then leave it on the review list. Service Bot: pull the open Zendesk or inbox queue and draft the safe replies. Scheduling Bot: read Google Calendar availability and propose times that do not collide. Ops Bot: log next action and owner where the signed-in tool allows, or prepare a copy to paste.

sources.pageTitle: Grok Bot for Role-Based Work in Your Tools
sources.text: What KCG configures Bot identity and job description for one role: sales follow-up, customer service, scheduling, or ops Signed-in tools limited to the systems that role needs, with narrow account access A taught routine for the first repeatable job, recorded before the Bot runs alone Review settings so customer-facing sends and sensitive record changes wait for a named person Optional team channels (Slack, Teams, or otherwise) only when the team already works there

sources.pageTitle: Grok Bot for Role-Based Work in Your Tools
sources.text: What you take away One named Bot with a written job, not a generic chatbot Documented sign-ins and review settings for sensitive actions A taught routine the owner can re-run Clear rule: the Bot drafts and prepares; a named human decides what leaves the business

sources.pageTitle: Grok Bot for Role-Based Work in Your Tools

sources.pageTitle: Grok Bot for Role-Based Work in Your Tools

sources.pageTitle: Grok Bot for Role-Based Work in Your Tools
sources.text: Connectors by time saved and input / output Grok Bot's strength is a computer that can sign into tools and a role you teach. Connections differ by account and site. xAI examples include Gmail, Google Calendar, GitHub, Zendesk, Google Docs, and review-gated outbound drafts. KCG does not claim identical email send or CRM write across every Bot.

sources.pageTitle: Grok Bot for Role-Based Work in Your Tools
sources.text: Gmail Scoped integration Time / rework saved Stops rebuilding quote history and outbound drafts by hand for the sales or service role. Input Signed-in Gmail plus the customer or ticket the owner names. Output Located thread, draft in the owner's voice, and a review list before send. xAI documents improved Gmail connections and draft-for-approval flows; KCG still requires a human before customer send.

sources.pageTitle: Grok Bot for Role-Based Work in Your Tools
sources.text: Google Calendar Scoped integration Time / rework saved Cuts back-and-forth when the scheduling role can read real availability. Input Signed-in calendar for the people or rooms in scope. Output Availability read and proposed times. Booking or invites wait for the reviewer when the action is sensitive.

sources.pageTitle: Grok Bot for Role-Based Work in Your Tools

Input Signed-in helpdesk or service tool the Bot can navigate like a person. Output Queue summary and reply drafts. Closing tickets or messaging customers stays behind review.

sources.pageTitle: Grok Bot for Role-Based Work in Your Tools
sources.text: Slack or Microsoft Teams (team interface) Scoped integration Time / rework saved Lets the team hand the Bot work where they already talk, without making chat the whole product. Input A question, handoff, or thread the role owns. Output Answers, drafts, or next-step lists in the channel. Sensitive actions still ask first.

sources.pageTitle: Grok Bot for Role-Based Work in Your Tools
sources.text: CRM write when no stable signed-in path exists Manual export Time / rework saved Keeps next action and owner from vanishing after the Bot finishes the packet. Input Agreed next action, owner, and due date. Output Paste-ready CRM note or import row. We do not invent native CRM write for every platform.

sources.pageTitle: Grok Bot for Role-Based Work in Your Tools
sources.text: Worked examples across industries Each example stays inside capabilities documented by the vendor. The assistant drafts. A named human decides.

sources.pageTitle: Grok Bot for Role-Based Work in Your Tools
sources.text: Sales follow-up Bot Equipment sales Problem Quotes go out, then die because nobody owns the second touch. Input Signed-in Gmail plus approved voice samples and the deal list the owner maintains. Draft Located approved quote, follow-up draft in the owner's voice, and a review list. Human decision Owner edits claims and prices, then approves which messages may send. Business benefit Sales follow-up becomes a named Bot job with a human gate, not a Slack novelty.

sources.pageTitle: Grok Bot for Role-Based Work in Your Tools
sources.text: Customer service queue Bot Consumer electronics retail Problem Routine warranty and order questions bury the messages that need a person. Input Signed-in Zendesk or inbox the Bot can work, plus approved answer material. Draft Prioritized queue with safe reply drafts and a short exception list. Human decision Reviewer releases routine replies and pulls exceptions to staff. The Bot does not close sensitive tickets alone. Business benefit Service capacity goes to judgment calls, while routine drafts stay reviewable.

sources.pageTitle: Grok Bot for Role-Based Work in Your Tools
sources.text: Scheduling Bot Dental / medical practice Problem Front desk rebuilds availability from memory while the phone is still ringing. Input Signed-in Google Calendar for the chairs or rooms in scope. Draft Open slots that do not collide, plus a confirmation draft for the reviewer. Human decision Front desk confirms the slot and only then sends the confirmation. Business benefit Scheduling uses real availability instead of a guessed calendar.

sources.pageTitle: Grok Bot for Role-Based Work in Your Tools
sources.text: Ops exception Bot Multi-location retail Problem Receiving mismatches and vendor credits die in private notes before close. Input Signed-in purchasing or receiving tools the Bot can access for the exception list. Draft Exception packet with proposed owner and next action. Human decision Ops lead assigns owners and logs the CRM or books update, using manual export when write is unavailable. Business benefit Ops follow-through has a named Bot and a named human closer.

sources.pageTitle: Grok Bot for Role-Based Work in Your Tools
sources.text: Good fit You can name one role and the tools that role already uses. Someone will teach the first routine from a real demo and own review for sensitive actions. You want an assistant that works in signed-in tools, not a chat widget that only answers FAQs.

sources.pageTitle: Grok Bot for Role-Based Work in Your Tools
sources.text: Poor fit You need Team Bots or meeting join on a plan that does not include them yet. You want unsupervised customer spam or record changes without review. Nobody will own the Bot's review list.

sources.pageTitle: Grok Bot for Role-Based Work in Your Tools
sources.text: Why it helps A shop does not need another generic chatbot. It needs a named role that can sign into the same tools a person would use, prepare the work, and stop for review before anything irreversible leaves.

sources.pageTitle: Grok Bot for Role-Based Work in Your Tools
sources.text: Pilot measurement Follow-ups or queue items drafted versus items that still needed full human reconstruction Time from Bot packet to reviewer decision Customer drafts prepared versus drafts approved to send Review rejections that caused a routine rewrite

sources.pageTitle: Grok Bot for Role-Based Work in Your Tools
sources.text: Limits Grok Bot needs an eligible plan and tool access. Team and Enterprise setups differ from an individual seat. Bots can take initiative, so review settings and narrow account access matter more than clever prompts. Teaching a task helps repeatability, but a bad demo teaches a bad routine. KCG records the steps before the Bot runs alone. Slack, Teams, and meeting join are optional interfaces. We only enable what the team will actually use. KCG does not install Bots into production accounts during a sales walkthrough.

sources.pageTitle: Grok Bot for Role-Based Work in Your Tools
sources.text: Named reviewer before actions Sensitive actions can go through review before they run. In a KCG setup, the named role owner is the reviewer for customer-facing drafts and any record changes the Bot prepares. sources.text: All services POS Placement New hardware. Zero check written. Replace the outdated terminal slowing your line without writing a check for hardware. sources.pageTitle: POS Placement
sources.text: The work keeps landing back on your desk. The terminal is the last thing a customer touches, and often the oldest technology in the building. If it embarrasses your brand, holds up the lunch rush or came with a hardware quote you cannot justify, replacement deserves a look. The equipment is paid for through processing, so no upfront hardware payment does not mean free card processing. The time cost is arithmetic, not a study result: extra seconds per transaction multiplied by transactions equals time spent waiting on the terminal. Measure your own counter before comparing equipment. New hardware cannot fix every delay, especially when the problem is the connection or how orders are entered.

sources.pageTitle: POS Placement
sources.text: Smart Terminals Let customers tap, insert a chip or use a supported mobile wallet such as Apple Pay. Customer-facing prompts handle tips and receipts so staff can finish the sale without fumbling with paper. We check the payment methods and receipt options on the proposed device before placement.

sources.pageTitle: POS Placement
sources.text: Full POS Systems Put the register, scanner, printer and cash drawer around how your business sells. Your team should not have to fight the software during a rush. We confirm which components are included and whether your inventory, menu or reporting needs require separate software before you switch.

sources.pageTitle: POS Placement
sources.text: Kitchen Display Systems Keep orders readable when paper tickets get lost, smeared or misread. Kitchen screens can route orders from a compatible POS and show preparation timers. We check station routing and order changes with your staff so the kitchen receives the information it needs.

sources.pageTitle: POS Placement
sources.text: Mobile & Wireless Readers Take payment tableside or at the front door when your counter also serves customers elsewhere. Wireless readers let staff bring checkout to the customer. We check coverage, charging and compatibility with the main register; a portable device still needs a suitable connection.

Sources: Federal Reserve, 2026 Report on Employer Firms (2025 survey)

sources.pageTitle: Prep To Sell
sources.text: All services Prep To Sell Build a business someone else can take over. A buyer needs to understand what they are buying and what keeps working after you leave. We help reduce owner dependence, document operations and organise the evidence behind revenue. For owners three to ten years from exit, preparation leaves time to test that independence. On this page What we build What is included The numbers The build process Common questions

sources.pageTitle: Prep To Sell
sources.text: The work keeps landing back on your desk. If every important customer calls your mobile and every exception waits for your decision, the business still depends heavily on you. We turn the question of how those relationships transfer into an operating plan before a sale depends on it.

sources.pageTitle: Prep To Sell
sources.text: Give the team responsibility they can carry Make routine decisions possible without asking the owner. We identify where work waits for your approval and define who can act, within what limits. A planned absence then tests the arrangement. The point is to find gaps early, while you can still coach the person taking over.

sources.pageTitle: Prep To Sell
sources.text: Make the financial story easier to verify Help advisers and prospective buyers follow the numbers back to their records. We organise the operating information and flag unexplained items for your accountant. Separating personal and business costs needs proper accounting treatment; we do not reclassify expenses to manufacture a more attractive earnings figure.

sources.pageTitle: Prep To Sell
sources.text: Document work people actually perform Keep essential knowledge available when someone changes roles. We capture important processes with the staff doing them, including exceptions and decision limits. Someone else then follows the instructions and reports what is missing. A folder of untested procedures does not prove the business can function independently.

sources.pageTitle: Prep To Sell
sources.text: Keep customer history with the business Make outstanding quotes and relationship history visible beyond the owner's phone. We improve CRM records and handoffs so staff can see commitments and next actions. A buyer can inspect the operating history, subject to appropriate access, instead of relying entirely on your recollection of each customer.

sources.pageTitle: Prep To Sell
sources.text: Show how revenue continues Organise evidence of repeat purchasing and genuine recurring agreements. We examine where revenue depends on a single relationship or on work only you can sell. Contract terms and transfer restrictions need adviser review. Repeat customers are valuable, but they should not be presented as contracted recurring revenue.

sources.pageTitle: Prep To Sell
sources.text: What a KCG build includes We scope operational preparation around your timeline. Transaction advice and formal valuation require the appropriate specialists. An owner-dependence review A map of responsibilities and relationships that still rely on you, prioritised by the disruption your absence would cause. A preparation roadmap Actions with owners and review dates, coordinated with your accountant and transaction advisers where they are involved. An operating evidence set Agreed process documents, CRM improvements and supporting records. Access stays controlled as commercially sensitive material is organised. Practical readiness checks Tests of delegation and handoffs, with gaps recorded for correction. The output is operating evidence, not a guaranteed valuation.

sources.text: Put a number on the time bought back Published research gives us a reason to measure. Your own results determine what the work is worth. 73%

sources.pageTitle: Prep To Sell

This is a dated survey horizon, not a fresh ten-year forecast from today. Sources: Exit Planning Institute, 2023 State of Owner Readiness findings (published 2024) $14 trillion

sources.pageTitle: Prep To Sell
sources.text: The estimated scale of those transitions The Exit Planning Institute estimated the private-business transition opportunity at $14 trillion in its 2023 findings. This is a market estimate, not completed sale proceeds or evidence of what your business is worth. Sources: Exit Planning Institute, 2023 State of Owner Readiness findings (published 2024)

sources.pageTitle: Prep To Sell
sources.text: Assess: start with your intended exit We discuss timing and your current role, then identify what would fail if you stepped away. Your advisers help define personal and transaction requirements.

sources.pageTitle: Prep To Sell

sources.pageTitle: Prep To Sell
sources.text: Test: let the team run the work Staff use the processes and customer records during agreed periods without your routine intervention. Exceptions show where decision rights or information are still missing.

sources.pageTitle: Prep To Sell

sources.pageTitle: Prep To Sell
sources.text: A good fit You are several years from exit and can delegate real responsibility now. You want records and systems that support continuity beyond the owner.

sources.pageTitle: Prep To Sell
sources.text: Not a good fit You need an immediate buyer or a guaranteed sale multiple. You want cosmetic financial changes while keeping every decision under your control.

sources.pageTitle: Prep To Sell
sources.text: How far ahead should I start? Enough time to change operations and show that the changes last. This service is aimed at owners three to ten years out, but we can discuss a shorter preparation window without promising the same scope.

sources.pageTitle: Prep To Sell
sources.text: Will this increase my sale price? Better records and lower dependence can address concerns buyers raise. Earnings and risk still matter, as does the market. We cannot promise a multiple or a buyer's response.

sources.pageTitle: Prep To Sell
sources.text: Are you the business broker? This engagement covers operational preparation. Listing the business, negotiating a transaction and providing formal legal, tax or valuation advice require separately appointed professionals.

sources.pageTitle: Prep To Sell
sources.text: Do we need recurring revenue? It can improve visibility where it fits the business. We examine the revenue you actually earn and any credible opportunities for repeat work. We do not relabel ordinary repeat sales as subscriptions.

sources.pageTitle: Prep To Sell
sources.text: What if I decide not to sell? Clear responsibilities and usable customer records still help you step back from daily firefighting. The preparation should leave a better-run operation even if your exit timeline changes.

sources.pageTitle: Prep To Sell
sources.text: How do we protect sensitive information? We agree who can access the working records and what is needed for each stage. Preparing information does not authorise sharing it with prospective buyers or external parties.

sources.pageTitle: Prep To Sell
sources.text: Find out what still depends on you. Tell Seth or Hunter your likely exit window and what happens when you take time away. We will discuss the first operational dependencies to address before a buyer reviews the business.

sources.text: How long does SEO take? Expect progress over months, with timing affected by your starting point and competition. Anyone guaranteeing page one in thirty days is promising a result they do not control.

sources.pageTitle: SEO Services
sources.text: Should I stop paying for ads? That depends on your existing results and demand needs. SEO can develop alongside paid traffic; we would not assume it can replace a channel that currently brings profitable work.

sources.pageTitle: Website Builds
sources.text: All services Website Builds Your website should be your best salesperson. Most sites sit there looking nice while the phone stays quiet. We build the other kind. The kind that stops the scroll, answers questions at 2 AM, and books the appointment before you ever pick up the phone. On this page What we build What is included The numbers The build process Common questions

sources.pageTitle: Website Builds
sources.text: The site is there. The enquiries are another matter. You send a prospect your website, then explain on the phone what the page should have made clear. Your work has improved. The site still describes the business you used to run. On a phone, the contact button is hard to find. A visitor has to pinch the screen to read the service details. Someone interested enough to click still has to work out how to buy. You want a site you can be proud to send people to. You also need it to answer practical questions and put an enquiry where your team will see it. A good-looking page that leaves that job unfinished is still unfinished.

sources.pageTitle: Website Builds
sources.text: Turn visits into calls with a custom business website Our core offering is a custom business website. We design around how your customer decides: what you do, why they should trust you, and how to get in touch. Most clients need this foundation first. What it replaces An outdated brochure site that leaves you explaining the basics on every call, or a template that buries the contact button. What you get Pages built to make the phone ring, with clear service details and a direct enquiry path. Mobile-first layouts and fast loading help people act from the screen they have. Who it is for Local businesses, trades and professional services that need customers to understand the offer and contact the team.

sources.pageTitle: Website Builds
sources.text: Turn a campaign click into a lead Lead-generating landing pages focus on a single offer. The page answers the reason someone clicked your ad, campaign or service link and gives them a clear next step. What it replaces Sending paid traffic to a general homepage, where visitors have to find the offer again. What you get A focused offer with supporting proof and a relevant enquiry form. We check that submissions reach the intended person and agree how to measure results. Who it is for Businesses running ads, promoting a specific service or testing an offer with a defined audience. Conversion is the goal, not a promised rate.

sources.pageTitle: Website Builds
sources.text: Let customers browse, buy and pay online E-commerce and online stores give customers a route from product catalogue to checkout. We organise products around how people shop and make the purchase steps clear. What it replaces Taking every order through messages, sending separate payment links, or making customers call to find out what you sell. What you get Product pages, a cart and checkout, plus an order flow your team can manage. Product options, stock handling, delivery and payment connections are agreed before the build. Who it is for Retailers and product businesses ready to sell online. Catalogue size and fulfilment needs determine the scope and platform.

sources.pageTitle: Website Builds
sources.text: Capture the job while the customer is ready Bookings, quotes and enquiries turn interest into a request your team can act on. We ask for the details you need to schedule an appointment or price the work. What it replaces Missed calls, vague contact messages and forms that land in an inbox nobody checks. What you get Booking systems, quote requests or service enquiry flows, with forms routed to the right person. We test confirmations and the handoff into your calendar or CRM where included. Who it is for Trades, clinics and appointment-based businesses, plus teams that need job details before they can quote.

sources.pageTitle: Website Builds
sources.text: Answer the next customer after closing time AI on the website gives visitors a chat or voice assistant that answers approved questions and captures leads outside business hours. With an agreed calendar connection, it can book appointments. What it replaces Waiting until morning to answer routine questions, or asking visitors to search through pages for a simple answer. What you get An assistant with defined answers and a clear handoff to your team when it is unsure. We scope the knowledge, booking access and ongoing usage fees before connecting it. Who it is for Businesses handling repeated pre-sale questions. Private account reviews and decisions requiring staff judgement stay with a person.

sources.pageTitle: Website Builds
sources.text: Help buyers inspect the details before they decide Interactive 3D and motion are specialist options. A customer can rotate a product or explore a space when photographs leave an important question unanswered. Scroll-driven motion can explain a product or process when movement helps. What it replaces Guessing at a product’s shape from a fixed angle, or leaving buyers without a way to explore a space they cannot visit yet. What you get A product viewer or purposeful motion, with mobile performance checks and a readable reduced-motion experience. A simple rotate-and-look viewer is often enough. Product-viewer research does not establish a return on decorative scroll animation. Who it is for E-commerce product pages, including furniture, apparel, footwear, jewellery or customisable products; real estate and property; automotive; equipment and machinery; hospitality venues. It is not right for every business. We will tell you when it is not worth the money

sources.pageTitle: Website Builds
sources.text: . Interactive 3D evidence What the product-viewer tests actually show Fibbl reports a 6.3% conversion uplift for GANT at 95% statistical significance. Nubikk saw add-to-cart rise 10.9% and visitors reaching checkout rise 21%, both at 99% certainty. These are footwear/apparel brand tests, not KCG results or universal forecasts. The gains are modest overall and can be stronger on mobile. Nubikk’s desktop transactions showed no measurable effect. Samples are limited and confidence intervals are wide. Novelty may inflate early results; the lift may shrink as 3D becomes standard. Brands investing in 3D often improve the rest of their digital experience too. The simple viewer carries most usage; extra effects need their own business case. Sources: Fibbl, GANT conversion study ; Fibbl, what the footwear A/B tests actually show

sources.pageTitle: Website Builds
sources.text: What a KCG build includes Every build starts with a written scope. We agree which work below your project needs, who supplies what, and what costs continue after launch. This is not an unlimited package. Strategy: give the visitor a clear next step We agree who the site is for, what they need to know and the main action they should take. That decision guides the pages we build. Design: look like the business customers will meet We design around your brand and your actual customers, not a template. You review layouts before they become finished pages. Copy: answer the questions that hold up a sale We write plain-language copy aimed at the agreed action. You confirm the facts; we remove filler and claims you cannot support. Build: make the site usable on every screen Responsive pages, fast loading and accessible navigation are part of the build. We check keyboard use, readable contrast and labelled forms alongside the mobile customer path. Technical foundations: be ready to be found We agree responsibility for hosting, domain setup and SSL

sources.pageTitle: Website Builds
sources.text: . Analytics, SEO structure and the sitemap are scoped alongside Google Business Profile setup or updates where relevant. Account fees are identified separately. AEO: answer the questions customers already ask Answer Engine Optimization means publishing clear answers to real customer questions as indexable service copy, for example "Do you serve Murray on Saturdays?" or "What is included in a furnace tune-up?" We structure hours, service area, pricing rules and contact facts so people and machines can read them. This is content and markup work. It is not a promise of AI citations or rankings. Integrations: get the enquiry where it belongs We scope booking, payments, CRM and email connections around the tools you use. Forms route to the agreed people, with test submissions before launch. Measurement is part of the same path: you can see whether enquiries arrived. Handover: own it and know how to use it You own the site and the accounts. We hand over access and train you to make simple edits using the agreed editing setup

sources.pageTitle: Website Builds
sources.text: Why speed belongs in the budget Published research gives us a reason to measure. Your own results determine what the work is worth. 53%

sources.pageTitle: Website Builds
sources.text: A reason to take mobile loading seriously Think with Google reports that this share of mobile visitors leaves a page taking longer than 3 seconds to load. This is historical research, not a measurement of your customers or a KCG result. Sources: Think with Google, Masters of Mobile report 20%

sources.pageTitle: Website Builds
sources.text: Speed has a conversion cost The Google report describes a drop in conversions for every second of mobile loading delay. This is a historical research finding, not a universal forecast. Making a page faster does not guarantee an equal increase in sales. Derived illustration: starting conversions × (1 − 20 / 100) = starting conversions × 0.80 after a second of delay. That leaves 80% of the starting total in this illustration. Sources: Think with Google, Masters of Mobile report 2.5 seconds

sources.pageTitle: Website Builds
sources.text: The performance targets we work toward Google’s good-experience thresholds are LCP within 2.5 seconds, INP under 200 milliseconds, and CLS under 0.1. LCP measures loading. INP measures responsiveness, while CLS measures visual stability. These are targets, not a claim that an untested build passes. Good scores alone do not guarantee rankings. Sources: Google Search Central, Core Web Vitals

sources.text: Discovery: agree on the customer path Show us the current site and explain what a good enquiry looks like. We review the pages you need and the material you already have. Seth and Hunter work directly with you to decide what belongs in the build.

sources.pageTitle: Website Builds
sources.text: Handover: know what you own You own the site. We walk through the agreed editing setup and hand over access. Hosting and any third-party assistant fees are identified separately so you know what continues after the build.

sources.text: A good fit You need your site to explain the work before a prospect calls. You can supply accurate service details and approve the pages with us. You want ownership of the site and a build shaped around your actual sales process.

sources.pageTitle: Website Builds
sources.text: Not a good fit You need a guaranteed ranking or sales figure before anyone has measured your traffic. You want animation everywhere even when it makes the site harder to use. You need a custom application outside these capabilities without a separate scope.

sources.pageTitle: Website Builds
sources.text: What does a website cost? We quote after reviewing the pages and connections you need. A focused landing page and a site with a voice assistant involve different work. We identify processing savings first and discuss reinvesting verified savings into the build. Savings are not assumed to cover the whole project.

sources.pageTitle: Website Builds
sources.text: How long will the build take? The schedule depends on the agreed scope and when content or account access is available. We set review points before work begins. We will not attach a stock turnaround promise to a project we have not looked at.

sources.pageTitle: Website Builds
sources.text: What if we already have a website? Send it to us. We review what is useful before recommending a replacement. Existing copy or photographs may carry over if you own them and they still describe the business accurately. We agree what changes before building.

sources.pageTitle: Website Builds
sources.text: Do I own it, and can I move it later? Yes. You own your site. We explain the handover and hosting arrangements in the scope, including what you need if another provider takes over later. Third-party subscriptions have their own terms, which we identify before you commit.

sources.pageTitle: Website Builds
sources.text: What is AEO on a KCG website build? AEO means Answer Engine Optimization: writing indexable answers to questions customers already ask, then structuring service facts so search systems can read them. Example questions include hours, coverage area, what a service includes, and how to book. We do not guarantee AI citations or rankings.

sources.pageTitle: Website Builds
sources.text: Can the site work with our current CRM? We check the form destination and the access your CRM allows before promising a connection. The goal is an enquiry arriving where the team already works. If the current system limits that handoff, we explain the options and scope the work.

sources.pageTitle: Website Builds
sources.text: How soon will it bring in customers? The site can accept enquiries once it is live and the contact path is tested. Generating demand is a separate question. We cannot promise a sales date or conversion lift. Your traffic and enquiry baseline give us a starting point for measurement, so any lift we report later is measured against your own numbers rather than a promise made now.

sources.pageTitle: Website Builds
sources.text: What do you need from us? An explanation of your services and access to whoever approves the content. We also need the brand material you have permission to use. For a rebuild, we identify the domain and hosting access needed before the launch date is agreed.

sources.pageTitle: Website Builds
sources.text: Show us the site you have outgrown. Send your current website and the part of the enquiry process that frustrates you. Seth or Hunter will discuss what needs rebuilding and where processing savings might help fund it.
